properties.decision: Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — dev_storyflow field report 2026-09-05, wish #26. get_node cost two round-trips to learn: unknown field `node_id`, then missing `node_type`. 'Requiring node_type as well is a second round-trip for every read.' WHAT IS CHEAP: node_type_index already resolves an id to its type for every detector, so a by-id read is one existing lookup away, and the typed-prefix convention is the documented reason ids are unique across types. A MIDDLE PATH: accept node_type as optional, resolve by index when omitted, and REFUSE (never guess) when an id resolves to more than one type — the one-call read for the common case, honesty for the collision.
properties.name: OPEN — get_node requires node_type as well as id, though the id prefix (`dec:`, `ver:`, `req:`) already names the type. Should a read resolve by id alone?
properties.rationale: THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is real: the prefix is a CONVENTION, not a rule — node_type_index's own comment says 'on a collision the first type scanned wins', so a by-id read on a graph with a convention violation would return a silently wrong node, which is worse than a required field. That is why the middle path refuses rather than picks. Part of the sibling-inconsistency class (fact:defect-sibling-constructors-disagree..., fact:defect-typed-tool-parameter-names-are-inconsistent): the read tools disagree with each other too.
